name: Vaitheeswaran Koil
deity: Shiva as Vaidyanatha (Vaitheeswaran), the divine healer, with Goddess Thaiyalnayaki (Balambika)
tradition: Shaiva; Navagraha Sthalam for Angaraka (Mars); Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Tevaram
period: Chola period, with later Nayak additions
summary: The healing shrine of the Navagraha circuit, where Shiva is worshipped as Vaidyanatha, the divine physician. Devotees come to pray for relief from illness and from Angaraka (Mars) affliction.

sections.history: Sung by the Tevaram saints, Vaitheeswaran Koil belongs to the revered Paadal Petra Sthalams, the shrines celebrated in early Tamil devotional hymns. The stone temple standing today took shape under the Cholas, with halls, shrines and the towering gopuram enriched by later Nayak patrons. Across the centuries its identity has been inseparable from healing: pilgrims have long carried their ailments here, trusting Shiva as Vaidyanatha to lift disease from the body. That reputation, echoed in the hymns and sustained by generations of vows, has made the temple one of the most visited healing shrines of the Kaveri delta.
sections.architecture: Built in the Dravidian idiom, the temple rises behind a tall gopuram and opens into pillared halls leading to the sanctum of Vaidyanatha. Separate shrines honour the Goddess Thaiyalnayaki and the child-god Muthukumaraswamy, the youthful Murugan much beloved here, while Angaraka, the planet Mars, is enshrined and worshipped within the complex. The sacred tank Siddhamirtham lies close by, its waters held to carry curative power. Stone corridors, subsidiary shrines and the weathered grace of Chola masonry give the temple the settled, lived-in feel of a place worn smooth by centuries of circumambulation and prayer.
sections.legends: The temple's lore binds it firmly to healing and to Mars. In one strand of tradition Angaraka, the planet Mars, was cured and blessed here, which is why the shrine anchors his station on the Navagraha pilgrimage. Devotees suffering skin ailments and disease bathe in the Siddhamirtham tank and offer jaggery, pepper and the sacred ash, thiruchandu, seeking Shiva's touch as the remover of affliction. The town also carries an association with Rama and the bird-king Jatayu. Above all, it is remembered as the place where the Lord, as divine physician, takes away the sickness of those who come in faith.
sections.festivals: Tuesdays, sacred to Angaraka, draw special worship, and pilgrims seeking relief from Mars affliction time their visits and vows accordingly. Pradosham is observed with care, and the martial devotion to Murugan finds its height at Skanda Sashti. The great festivals of the Tamil months of Thai and Panguni fill the streets with processions. Throughout the calendar, healing vows and the abhishekam bathing of the deity remain the heart of worship, with families returning to fulfil promises made in times of sickness.
sections.experience: Arriving pilgrims often bathe first in the Siddhamirtham tank before entering, carrying offerings of jaggery, pepper and holy ash. Inside, the mood is quietly earnest rather than grand: people move slowly, many nursing an illness or a family worry, and the air holds the settled hush of a place devoted to healing. The nearby town is also known for its Nadi astrology palm-leaf readings, which bring a steady stream of curious visitors. Move gently, keep to the flow of circumambulation, and give way to the elderly and unwell who come here above all seeking relief.

visit.timings: Roughly 6:00 am to 1:00 pm and 4:00 pm to 8:30 pm; verify locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected; cover shoulders and knees.
visit.photography: Photography inside the sanctum is generally not permitted; observe posted signs and staff instructions.
visit.gettingThere: In Vaitheeswaran Koil town, Mayiladuthurai district, near Sirkazhi, about 25 km from Mayiladuthurai in Tamil Nadu. The town has its own railway station on the Mayiladuthurai–Tharangambadi line; the nearest airport is Tiruchirappalli, about 150 km away.
